wv_1_tan_wall.blurb: A compact sandstone cliff in the Lower Meadow section of the Meadow River Gorge, easy to walk past without noticing. It holds about two dozen lines split fairly evenly between bolted sport climbs and routes that want a trad rack, and several of the routes mix the two styles. Grades start in the 5.4 range and climb to a few 5.12s, with the bulk of the climbing between 5.5 and 5.10, so there is something for newer leaders and for people chasing harder lines. The wall is short and the walk in is among the quickest in the gorge, which makes it a handy quick stop. Guided groups sometimes fill it.

wv_08_iceberg_area.blurb: The Iceberg is a big detached block of sandstone at Bozoo in southern West Virginia, sitting just upstream of the camp field. Climbs run up its front face and along a cool, shaded passage behind it. Most of the twenty-odd lines are traditional, with a handful of bolted routes and one boulder problem, and many can be set up as top ropes. Grades run from easy 5.6 and 5.7 through the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with one 5.12 at the hard end. Bolts on some of the sport lines are widely spaced, and the rock is solid. The easier top-rope lines work well for introducing beginners.
wv_08_iceberg_area.approach: From the camp field, take the trail that leaves its far right corner and stay on the right-hand branch. The Iceberg is the first cliff you reach, around five minutes in.

wv_m_fantasy_area.blurb: One of the sectors of Endless Wall in the New River Gorge, known as a comparatively cool place to climb in summer. About two dozen sandstone lines are split evenly between bolted sport routes and trad climbs. The grades lean hard: a few climbs in the 5.8 range, then mostly 5.11 and low 5.12, with one 5.13 on top. A well-known 5.8 crack in the sector gives moderate climbers a way in, while the steeper sport lines suit those working the 5.11 and 5.12 grades. Reaching the base means either a short hike along the cliff base or a rappel that needs a long rope.

wv_3_the_brain.blurb: The first real cliff you meet along the hike on Beauty Mountain, above the New River Gorge near Fayetteville. The main feature is a jutting, undercut buttress of sandstone, with blank rock low down and vertical runnels higher up. About twenty routes, mostly bolted with some trad: a few moderate lines from 5.7 to 5.10, then a good cluster of 5.12s through 5.14. Just beyond the buttress, the sport climbing gets steeper and harder, and around the corner is one of the gorge's densest collections of 5.14 climbs. A good stop for strong sport climbers, with a few easier options too.

wv_ballard_trail_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of sandstone boulders and low outcrops up the Ballard Trail in Kanawha State Forest, outside Charleston. It is more of a local training spot than a destination, but the rock is kind to the skin and the place rarely gets busy. Most of the roughly twenty problems are bouldering, covering everything from VB and V0 up through V7, with the middle of the range around V2 to V4. A few top-rope lines, mostly 5.9 to 5.11, share the same rocks. Bring a pad; the climbing is short and sits at the upper switchback of the trail.
